Pele Yoetz 391:1: Teshuah (Salvation) - The salvation of the Lord comes in the blink of an eye, and one of the questions a person is asked on the day of judgment is, "Did you hope for salvation?" (Midrash Mishlei Rabbati, ch. 10). And as we have written above under the entry Tzipiyah, see there. And it is not only for salvation from the exile that one must sit and wait, but regarding every trouble, that it not come, he should trust in the Name and rely on his God to save him from his trouble - and one who truly trusts in the Lord, as we have written above under the entry Havtachah, the kindness of the Lord shall surround him. And it has already been written in the name of the Ari that when a person says every day in the Amidah prayer, "For Your salvation we hope all day long," he should also intend this in general toward the specific trouble he stands in on that day, that he is hoping for the salvation of the Lord - and there is wondrous benefit in this. And it is already said (Proverbs 21:31), "The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but salvation is the Lord's." For it is true that an obligation rests upon a person to make every effort within his power, whether through himself or through others, to be saved from his trouble by natural means - but he should not trust in his own efforts, nor should he assume that whatever seems good in his own eyes is what he himself must accomplish; rather, it is the Lord who places it in the hearts of His creatures to fulfill His will, or not to fulfill it, when He does not wish salvation to come to that person through them - either because it is good for him that they act as they do, or because the Name wishes him to be somewhat drawn out in suffering for the atonement of his sins, and that his salvation come through another, for the Omnipresent has many agents, and He brings merit about through one who is meritorious. And let every person learn from our father Jacob, who prepared himself with a gift, with conciliation, with battle, and with prayer - and this is a great principle for being saved from any trouble: that both effort and prayer are necessary, and one without the other does not suffice. And after doing all these things as much as is in his power to do, let him wait for the salvation of the Name, for without any doubt, whatever the Merciful One does, He does for the good, and to Him are calculated all the workings, and in the end honor shall come.
